key_insight: Spherical propeller forcing produces a purely forward energy cascade across scale space, while energy flux remains direction-dependent despite a highly isotropic energy distribution.
engineering_relevance: The proposed framework links propeller frequency to key turbulence variables, supporting the design and operation of nearly homogeneous, isotropic turbulence chambers.
method: Analyze scale-by-scale energy transfer using the Kármán–Howarth–Monin framework without assuming isotropy.
Measure temporal turbulence statistics under low-mean-flow conditions where Taylor’s frozen-turbulence hypothesis does not apply.
Relate turbulent scales to propeller frequency using measurements from this device and previously reported HIT chambers.
evidence_signal: Measurements show orientation-averaged structure functions consistent with Kolmogorov’s two-thirds law and an intermediate-scale Eulerian frequency spectrum consistent with Tennekes’ prediction.
watch_item: Residual forcing asymmetries affect directional energy flux, so isotropic energy statistics alone do not establish isotropic interscale transfer.
paper_title: Interscale energy transfer in a propeller-driven homogeneous and isotropic turbulence generation device
